_meta.description: Exercise form cues, technique tips, warmup recommendations, and common mistakes for gym exercises. Matches Hevy naming conventions.
_meta.usage: Triggered when Hevy sync detects a user performing an exercise for the first time (no prior history). Sent as form coaching via Telegram.

technique_cues: Retract and depress shoulder blades — pinch them together and down
Plant feet flat on the floor, drive through heels for leg drive
Grip bar slightly wider than shoulder width — wrists stacked over elbows
Lower bar to nipple line with controlled tempo (2-3 seconds down)
Press up and slightly back toward the rack — bar path is a slight J-curve
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows to 90° (keep ~45-75° angle to protect shoulders)
Bouncing bar off chest instead of pausing briefly at bottom
Lifting hips off the bench — maintain arch but keep glutes planted
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 2 sets of 10 with empty bar, then 1 set at 50% working weight, 1 set at 75%
exercises.muscle_activation: Chest stretch at the bottom, strong chest and tricep squeeze at lockout

technique_cues: Start with dumbbells on thighs, kick them up one at a time as you lie back
Retract shoulder blades and maintain a slight arch
Lower dumbbells to chest level with palms facing forward
Press up, allowing a slight inward arc at the top for chest squeeze
Keep wrists neutral — don't let them bend backward
common_mistakes: Going too deep and overstretching the shoulder joint
Using asymmetric range of motion (one arm lower than the other)
Dropping dumbbells to the side at end of set — kick knees up, sit forward
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 12 at 50% working weight, 1 set of 8 at 75%
exercises.muscle_activation: Deep chest stretch at bottom, peak contraction when dumbbells come together at top

technique_cues: Set bench to 30-45° angle — lower angle = more chest, higher = more shoulders
Retract shoulder blades against the bench pad
Lower bar to upper chest / clavicle area
Press straight up — bar path is more vertical than flat bench
Keep feet planted and maintain back contact with bench
common_mistakes: Setting bench too steep (>45°) which turns it into a shoulder press
Letting the bar drift forward over the face
Losing shoulder blade retraction as the set progresses
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 10 with empty bar on incline, 1 set at 60% working weight
exercises.muscle_activation: Upper chest and front delts — feel the stretch across upper pecs at bottom

technique_cues: Set bench to 30-45° incline
Kick dumbbells up and press to start position before beginning reps
Lower with control to upper chest level, elbows at ~45° from torso
Press up with slight inward arc for upper chest contraction
Maintain shoulder blade retraction throughout
common_mistakes: Using momentum to swing dumbbells up instead of controlled press
Flaring elbows to 90° on the descent
Arching excessively — keep lower back on the bench
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 12 at 50% working weight
exercises.muscle_activation: Strong upper chest and front deltoid engagement throughout the press

technique_cues: Set cables to appropriate height — high for lower chest, mid for mid, low for upper
Step forward into a staggered stance for stability
Maintain a slight bend in elbows throughout — arms should look like hugging a tree
Squeeze chest hard at the midpoint, control the return
Focus on the stretch — feel pecs lengthening on the eccentric
common_mistakes: Bending elbows too much, turning it into a press instead of a fly
Using too much weight and losing the stretch/squeeze
Leaning too far forward and using body momentum
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 light set of 15 to establish mind-muscle connection
exercises.muscle_activation: Deep chest stretch at full extension, intense chest squeeze at contraction point

technique_cues: Lean torso forward ~30° to target chest over triceps
Grip bars slightly wider than shoulder width if adjustable
Lower until upper arms are parallel to floor or slight stretch in chest
Press up by squeezing chest — don't just push with triceps
Keep elbows angled slightly outward (not flared, not tucked)
common_mistakes: Staying upright (this targets triceps instead of chest)
Going too deep and stressing the shoulder joint
Swinging or kipping — keep movement controlled
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 8-10 bodyweight dips at controlled tempo
exercises.muscle_activation: Lower chest stretch at bottom, chest and tricep engagement at top

technique_cues: Hands slightly wider than shoulder width, fingers pointing forward
Body forms a straight line from head to heels — engage core and glutes
Lower chest to 1 inch from floor with elbows at ~45° angle
Push through palms, fully extend arms at top
Protract shoulder blades at top for serratus anterior activation
common_mistakes: Sagging hips or piking them up — maintain rigid plank position
Flaring elbows straight out to the sides (injury risk)
Only doing partial reps — go to full depth
exercises.warmup_recommendation: Perform as warmup exercise: 2 sets of 10-15 before pressing movements
exercises.muscle_activation: Chest, front delts, and triceps — should feel across the entire chest

technique_cues: Feet hip-width apart, bar over mid-foot — shins nearly touching bar
Hinge at hips and grip bar just outside knees (double overhand or mixed grip)
Flatten back, chest up, take slack out of the bar before pulling
Drive through the floor with legs first, then extend hips — bar stays close to body
Lock out by squeezing glutes at top — don't hyperextend the lower back
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back — this is the #1 injury risk, keep it neutral
Starting with hips too low (it's not a squat) or too high (stiff-leg)
Jerking the bar off the floor instead of building tension first
exercises.warmup_recommendation: Hip hinges × 10, then 135 lbs × 5, then 60% × 5, then 80% × 3
exercises.muscle_activation: Entire posterior chain — hamstrings and glutes drive the lift, erectors stabilize

technique_cues: Hinge at hips to ~45° torso angle, slight knee bend
Grip bar shoulder-width, pull to lower chest/upper abs
Lead with elbows — drive them behind you, squeeze shoulder blades together
Control the negative — don't just let the weight drop
Keep core braced to protect lower back throughout
common_mistakes: Standing too upright, turning it into an upright row
Using momentum and body English to swing the weight up
Not fully contracting at the top — row until bar touches torso
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 10 with just the bar, 1 set at 50% working weight
exercises.muscle_activation: Lats, rhomboids, and rear delts — feel the squeeze between shoulder blades at top

technique_cues: Grip bar slightly wider than shoulder width — overhand grip
Sit tall, lean back slightly (~10-15°), chest up
Pull bar to upper chest, driving elbows down and back
Squeeze lats at the bottom — imagine putting your elbows in your back pockets
Control the bar back up — full stretch at top, feel lats lengthening
common_mistakes: Leaning too far back and turning it into a row
Pulling with biceps instead of initiating with lats
Using momentum — yanking the weight down and letting it snap back up
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 12-15 at light weight to feel the lat stretch and contraction
exercises.muscle_activation: Lats primarily — you should feel the stretch at the top and contraction at the bottom

technique_cues: Grip bar slightly wider than shoulder width, overhand grip
Start from a dead hang — full arm extension, shoulders engaged (not relaxed)
Pull by driving elbows down — chin clears the bar at the top
Control the descent — don't just drop down
Avoid excessive kipping — strict form builds more strength
common_mistakes: Not going to full extension at the bottom (partial reps)
Craning neck to get chin over bar instead of actually pulling higher
Swinging and using momentum (unless intentionally doing kipping pull-ups)
exercises.warmup_recommendation: Dead hangs for 15-20 seconds, then 1 set of scapular pull-ups (just shrug up from hang)
exercises.muscle_activation: Lats, biceps, and rear delts — feel lats engage as primary mover

technique_cues: Sit upright with slight lean forward to start — knees slightly bent
Pull handle to lower chest/upper abs, driving elbows straight back
Squeeze shoulder blades together at peak contraction — 1 second hold
Return with control, allowing a slight stretch forward but don't round the back
Keep chest proud throughout the movement
common_mistakes: Excessive body rocking back and forth to generate momentum
Rounding the back on the stretch portion
Shrugging shoulders up instead of pulling elbows back
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 12-15 at light weight focusing on the squeeze
exercises.muscle_activation: Mid-back (rhomboids), lats, and rear delts — feel the contraction between shoulder blades

technique_cues: Straddle the bar, hinge at hips to ~45° torso angle
Use a close-grip handle — pull toward chest
Drive elbows past torso, squeeze at the top
Keep core tight to protect lower back
Control the eccentric — don't bounce at the bottom
common_mistakes: Standing too upright, reducing back engagement
Using lower back to jerk the weight up instead of pulling with lats
Not getting full range of motion — pull until handle touches chest
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 10 at 50% working weight, focus on lat engagement
exercises.muscle_activation: Thick mid-back contraction — lats, rhomboids, traps, and rear delts

technique_cues: One hand and knee on bench, opposite foot on floor for stability
Let the dumbbell hang straight down, then row to hip/lower rib
Drive elbow up and back — think pulling a lawn mower cord
Rotate torso slightly at top for extra range of motion
Lower with control — full stretch at bottom, lat fully lengthened
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso excessively to cheat the weight up
Rowing to the armpit instead of the hip (too much shoulder, not enough lat)
Using too heavy a weight and losing control of the movement
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 10 per side at light weight to establish the movement pattern
exercises.muscle_activation: Unilateral lat engagement — feel the stretch at bottom and squeeze at hip level

technique_cues: Grip bar just outside shoulder width, bar resting on front delts
Brace core hard — squeeze glutes to prevent lower back arch
Press straight up, moving head slightly back to let bar pass, then forward once bar clears
Lock out directly overhead — bar should be over mid-foot at top
Lower with control back to front delt starting position
common_mistakes: Excessive lower back arch — this means the weight is too heavy or core isn't braced
Pressing the bar forward instead of straight overhead
Not using full range of motion — bar should touch delts at bottom
exercises.warmup_recommendation: Empty bar × 10, then 50% × 8, then 75% × 5. Include arm circles and band pull-aparts.
exercises.muscle_activation: Front and lateral delts, with triceps at lockout — shoulders should burn, not lower back

technique_cues: Stand with slight forward lean, dumbbells at sides
Raise arms out to the sides until parallel with floor — lead with elbows
Slight bend in elbows throughout (not straight arms, not bent rows)
Think about pouring water out of a pitcher at the top (pinkies slightly higher)
Lower with control — 2-3 second negative for maximum tension
common_mistakes: Using too much weight and swinging — this is a light, controlled exercise
Shrugging traps to get the weight up (keep shoulders down)
Raising too high above shoulder level — parallel is sufficient
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 15-20 with very light weight (5-10 lbs) to pre-exhaust and warm the joint
exercises.muscle_activation: Lateral deltoid burn — should feel it on the outside of the shoulder cap

technique_cues: Set cable at upper chest to face height with rope attachment
Pull rope toward face, separating the ends as you pull
At end position, hands should be beside your ears, elbows high and back
Squeeze rear delts and external rotators at peak contraction — 2 second hold
Keep upper arms parallel to the floor throughout
common_mistakes: Using too much weight and turning it into a row
Not separating the rope — just pulling it straight to the face
Leaning back excessively to move the weight
exercises.warmup_recommendation: Use face pulls as a warmup: 2 sets of 15-20 before any pressing day
exercises.muscle_activation: Rear delts, rhomboids, and external rotators — essential for shoulder health

technique_cues: Start with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing you (like the top of a curl)
As you press up, rotate palms outward so they face forward at the top
Full lockout overhead with palms facing away from you
Reverse the rotation on the way down — palms face you at bottom
Keep the rotation smooth and continuous — don't pause mid-rotation
common_mistakes: Rushing the rotation — the controlled twist IS the exercise
Not pressing to full lockout overhead
Arching the lower back — keep core tight, use a bench with back support if needed
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 10 with light dumbbells (10-15 lbs) to groove the rotation pattern
exercises.muscle_activation: All three deltoid heads through the rotation — front delts, lateral delts at top

technique_cues: Hinge at hips, torso nearly parallel to floor (or use an incline bench face-down)
Let dumbbells hang below with slight elbow bend
Raise arms out to the sides, squeezing shoulder blades together at top
Lead with elbows — think spreading your wings
Lower slowly — 2-3 second eccentric for maximum rear delt work
common_mistakes: Standing too upright (turns into a lateral raise)
Using momentum to swing the weight up
Shrugging traps instead of isolating rear delts
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 15 with very light weight — rear delts are small muscles
exercises.muscle_activation: Rear deltoids and upper back — feel the squeeze between shoulder blades

technique_cues: Bar position: high bar (on traps) or low bar (on rear delts) — pick one and be consistent
Feet shoulder-width or slightly wider, toes angled out 15-30°
Brace core hard — big breath into belly, hold it throughout rep (valsalva)
Break at hips and knees simultaneously, sit down between your legs
Hit parallel (hip crease at or below knee) — drive up through mid-foot
common_mistakes: Knees caving inward (valgus) — push knees out in line with toes
Rising hips first causing a 'good morning squat' — keep chest up
Not hitting depth — half squats don't count and overload the knees
exercises.warmup_recommendation: Bodyweight squats × 15, empty bar × 10, 50% × 8, 75% × 5, 90% × 2
exercises.muscle_activation: Quads, glutes, and adductors — feel quads stretch at bottom, glutes drive at top

technique_cues: Hinge at hips, not waist — push hips back as if closing a car door with your butt
Keep bar close to shins and thighs throughout the descent
Slight knee bend (15-20°) — this is NOT a stiff-leg deadlift
Feel the deep stretch in hamstrings at the bottom — go as low as flexibility allows
Squeeze glutes hard to return to standing — lock out hips at top
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back — maintain neutral spine, keep chest proud
Going too heavy too soon — master the hip hinge pattern first
Bending knees too much, turning it into a conventional deadlift
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 2 sets of 10 bodyweight hip hinges, then 1 set of 8 at 50% working weight
exercises.muscle_activation: Deep hamstring stretch at the bottom, strong glute squeeze at the top

technique_cues: Foot placement: mid-platform shoulder-width for balanced quad/glute work
Higher feet = more glute/hamstring; lower feet = more quad (but more knee stress)
Lower sled until knees are at ~90° — don't let lower back round off the pad
Press through the whole foot — don't just push with toes
Don't lock out knees at top — keep slight bend to maintain tension
common_mistakes: Going too deep and letting the lower back curl off the pad (butt wink)
Locking out knees completely at the top (dangerous under heavy load)
Using a too-narrow foot stance that stresses the knees
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 15 at 40% working weight to warm up the knee joint
exercises.muscle_activation: Quads primarily (with lower foot placement) or quads + glutes (higher placement)

technique_cues: Adjust pad to sit just above your ankles, not on the shins
Sit back fully in the seat, grip the handles
Extend legs to full lockout — squeeze quads hard at the top for 1 second
Lower with control — 3 second negative for maximum quad tension
Keep hips planted — don't use momentum to swing the weight
common_mistakes: Using too much weight and swinging — this is an isolation exercise
Not reaching full extension at the top — lock it out for peak contraction
Lifting hips off the seat to generate momentum
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 15 at light weight — great as a pre-activation exercise before squats
exercises.muscle_activation: Pure quadriceps isolation — burn should be in the front of the thigh

technique_cues: Adjust pad to sit just above your heels (Achilles area)
Lying: lie flat, grab handles, keep hips pressed into pad
Curl heels toward glutes — squeeze hamstrings at peak contraction
Lower slowly — 3 second eccentric for full stretch
Don't let hips rise off the pad to assist the curl
common_mistakes: Lifting hips off the pad to help curl (means weight is too heavy)
Only doing partial reps — full range from nearly straight to full curl
Rushing the negative — the eccentric is where growth happens
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 15 at light weight to warm up hamstrings before heavy leg work
exercises.muscle_activation: Hamstring isolation — feel the contraction behind the thigh, especially at peak curl

technique_cues: Rear foot on bench, laces down — front foot about 2 feet ahead of bench
Lower straight down until rear knee nearly touches floor
Front shin should stay relatively vertical — knee over ankle, not past toes
Drive up through the front heel — focus on the front leg doing all the work
Keep torso upright — slight forward lean is OK for glute emphasis
common_mistakes: Standing too close to the bench (knee goes past toes, stresses joint)
Standing too far from the bench (hip flexor strain on rear leg)
Losing balance — use a fixed bench, start with bodyweight to find position
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 8 per leg bodyweight only, then light dumbbells for 1 set of 8
exercises.muscle_activation: Front leg quads and glutes — you should feel this in the working leg, not the rear one

technique_cues: Upper back against bench, feet flat on floor about hip-width apart
Bar padded and positioned in hip crease — roll it into position
Drive hips up by squeezing glutes — full hip extension at top
Hold top position for 1-2 seconds with maximal glute squeeze
Chin tucked slightly — look forward, not up at the ceiling
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top instead of using glutes
Feet too close or too far from body — knees should be ~90° at top
Not reaching full hip extension — squeeze until you feel glutes cramp
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 15 bodyweight glute bridges, then 1 set at 50% working weight
exercises.muscle_activation: Pure glute contraction — if you feel lower back, you're hyperextending

technique_cues: Balls of feet on the edge of the platform, heels hanging off
Rise up onto toes as high as possible — full contraction at the top
Hold the top for 1-2 seconds — squeeze the calves
Lower slowly — let heels drop below the platform level for full stretch
Keep knees straight (slight bend OK) to target the gastrocnemius
common_mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom instead of controlled full range of motion
Not going through full range — both the stretch and the contraction matter
Bending knees excessively (shifts work to soleus — do seated calf raise for that)
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 20 bodyweight calf raises to warm up the Achilles tendon
exercises.muscle_activation: Gastrocnemius (upper calf) — feel the stretch at bottom and peak contraction at top

technique_cues: Stand upright, grip bar shoulder-width with underhand grip
Keep elbows pinned to your sides — they should not drift forward
Curl the bar up in an arc, squeezing biceps at the top
Lower with control — 2-3 second eccentric, full extension at bottom
Don't swing your body — if you need to, the weight is too heavy
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso back to cheat the weight up
Elbows drifting forward (shifts work to front delts)
Not going to full extension at the bottom — stretch the biceps
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 12 with just the bar or very light weight
exercises.muscle_activation: Biceps peak contraction at the top, full stretch at the bottom

technique_cues: Hold dumbbells with neutral grip (palms facing each other) at sides
Curl up keeping palms facing each other throughout — no rotation
Can alternate arms or curl both simultaneously
Squeeze at the top — feel the brachialis and forearm engagement
Lower with control — don't let gravity do the work
common_mistakes: Rotating wrists during the curl (that's a regular dumbbell curl)
Swinging dumbbells with body momentum
Not using full range of motion at the bottom
exercises.warmup_recommendation: Part of arm day warmup: 1 set of 12 at light weight
exercises.muscle_activation: Brachialis (under the biceps) and brachioradialis (forearm) — builds arm thickness

technique_cues: Sit at preacher bench, upper arm flat against the angled pad
Start with arm fully extended — feel the biceps stretch at the bottom
Curl dumbbell up, squeezing biceps at the top
Lower slowly — the stretch at the bottom is where the magic happens
Don't let the elbow lift off the pad at any point
common_mistakes: Not going to full extension (scared of the stretch — use lighter weight)
Lifting elbows off the pad to cheat the weight up
Going too heavy — this is a strict isolation movement
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 12 per arm at light weight — the preacher curl stretch requires warm biceps
exercises.muscle_activation: Biceps long head emphasis — strong stretch at bottom, peak contraction at top

technique_cues: Stand close to the cable, slight forward lean, elbows pinned to sides
Push the bar/rope down until arms are fully extended — squeeze triceps
Only the forearms should move — upper arms stay stationary
Return with control to ~90° elbow bend — don't let the weight stack slam
If using rope, split the ends apart at the bottom for extra contraction
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring forward or drifting away from the body
Leaning over the weight and using body weight to push down
Not reaching full lockout — extend completely for peak tricep contraction
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 15 at light weight — great warmup before heavy pressing
exercises.muscle_activation: Triceps lateral and medial heads — feel the squeeze at full extension

technique_cues: Lie on flat bench, press bar up to start — arms extended over upper chest
Keep upper arms perpendicular to the floor (or slightly tilted back toward head)
Bend only at elbows — lower bar toward forehead or just behind the top of head
Extend arms back to start by squeezing triceps — don't flare elbows
Use EZ bar to reduce wrist strain
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring out wide (stresses the joint, reduces tricep isolation)
Moving the upper arm — only the forearm should move at the elbow joint
Using too much weight — this exercise stresses the elbow joint, go moderate
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 10 with just the EZ bar to warm up elbows, then 1 set at 50%
exercises.muscle_activation: Triceps long head emphasis — feel the stretch when bar is behind the head

technique_cues: Forearms on floor, elbows directly under shoulders
Body forms a perfectly straight line from head to heels
Engage core by pulling belly button toward spine — brace like expecting a punch
Squeeze glutes to prevent hip sag
Breathe steadily — don't hold your breath
common_mistakes: Hips sagging toward the floor (means core is fatigued — stop or regress)
Piking hips up too high (easier but defeats the purpose)
Looking forward/up instead of down (strains the neck)
exercises.warmup_recommendation: Use as a core activation drill: 2 × 20-30 seconds before compound lifts
exercises.muscle_activation: Entire core — transverse abdominis, rectus abdominis, obliques, and erectors

technique_cues: Hang from pull-up bar with overhand grip, arms fully extended
Curl pelvis up by raising legs — focus on posterior pelvic tilt, not just lifting legs
Raise legs to at least parallel with floor — higher is better for lower abs
Lower with control — 3 second negative, don't just swing down
Minimize body swing — if swinging, slow down or use a captain's chair
common_mistakes: Just lifting legs without curling the pelvis (hip flexors do the work, not abs)
Swinging and using momentum — this should be slow and controlled
Dropping legs quickly on the descent
exercises.warmup_recommendation: Dead hangs for 15 seconds, then 1 set of knee raises (bent-leg version) × 10
exercises.muscle_activation: Lower abdominals and hip flexors — feel the abs contract when the pelvis tilts

technique_cues: Kneel in front of cable, hold rope behind head at forehead level
Crunch down by flexing the spine — bring elbows toward knees
Focus on curling the torso, not just bending at the hips
Squeeze the abs at the bottom of the crunch — hold 1 second
Return to starting position with control — feel the abs stretch
common_mistakes: Sitting back onto heels (makes it a hip flexion, not a crunch)
Using arms to pull the weight instead of crunching with abs
Not controlling the movement — using momentum to swing
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 15 at light weight to establish the mind-muscle connection
exercises.muscle_activation: Upper and mid abs — the loaded crunch pattern under resistance

technique_cues: Start on knees, hands gripping the ab wheel directly under shoulders
Brace core HARD — this is a full anti-extension exercise
Roll out as far as you can while maintaining a flat back — no lower back sag
Arms extend overhead as you roll out — full body stretch
Pull back by contracting abs — imagine pulling your belly button to spine
common_mistakes: Lower back sagging during the rollout (means you went too far — shorten range)
Using arms to pull back instead of abs
Going too far too soon — build up range of motion gradually
exercises.warmup_recommendation: Start with partial rollouts (only go out halfway) for the first set of 5-8
exercises.muscle_activation: Full anterior core — abs work hard to prevent spinal extension under load

technique_cues: Use a V-bar or close-grip handle attachment
Sit tall, lean back slightly, chest up
Pull handle to upper chest, driving elbows down to your sides
Squeeze lats hard at the bottom — 1 second hold
Control the weight back up — full stretch at the top
common_mistakes: Using too much body lean to move the weight
Pulling with biceps instead of initiating with lats
Not getting full range of motion — stretch at top, squeeze at bottom
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 12 at light weight to feel the lat engagement
exercises.muscle_activation: Lower lats with more bicep involvement due to close grip — feel contraction low on the back

technique_cues: Place one foot in the center of the platform, other foot off to the side
Lower sled with control until knee reaches ~90° bend
Press through the heel and mid-foot — full extension without lockout
Keep hips even — don't let the working side rotate
Use significantly less weight than bilateral leg press
common_mistakes: Going too heavy — start with 40% of bilateral leg press weight per leg
Letting the knee cave inward — push knee out in line with toes
Not using full range of motion to each side equally
exercises.warmup_recommendation: 1 set of 10 per leg at very light weight to warm up unilaterally
exercises.muscle_activation: Unilateral quad and glute engagement — exposes and corrects strength imbalances
